chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man contracted a buy-back deal (ta'yin), then his debt became due, but he could not find what to pay it with. Can he contract another buy-back from his companion whom he had contracted the first buy-back with, and pay it? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.
ai.seo_question: Can a debtor renew a buy-back deal with the same creditor if he cannot pay the original debt?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of renewing a 'buy-back' (bay' al-ta'zir) agreement when a debtor, though technically freed from the initial obligation, lacks the liquidity to pay off the debt in full. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that the debtor may designate the same creditor for a new deferred payment arrangement, ensuring continuity in debt settlement without invalidating the previous transaction. This ruling highlights the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence to accommodate debtors' financial constraints while preserving the creditor's rights.
